title: Supabase backend setup: the database behind my Vercel projects
hook: This one's going to be all about Supabase
guide: Add a database to a web app with Supabase and Vercel, so your site can save and read data (for example, reports users create). You need a free Supabase account, a Vercel account, and a web project hosted on Vercel.
1. Create a new project in Supabase and choose a region close to your users.
1. Open the Supabase table editor and create a table for what you want to store, such as reports, with a column for each field.
1. Copy the project URL and the public (anon) key from the Supabase project settings.
1. Add both values as environment variables in your Vercel project settings.
1. Install the Supabase client library in your web app and connect it using those two variables.
1. Change your app to save and load that data through Supabase instead of keeping it only on the page.
1. Deploy on Vercel and check that the saved data appears in the Supabase table editor.
Watch out: keep secret keys (the service role key) out of your front-end code and only ever put the public key in the browser.

```
You are helping me add a database backend to my web app using Supabase, deployed on Vercel. My app is <describe your app, e.g. a site where users create and view reports>, built with <framework, e.g. Next.js>. I have a Supabase account and a Vercel account, and my code is in <GitHub repo or local folder>.
Please:
1. Design a simple table schema for <what I want to store> and give me the SQL to create it in Supabase.
2. Show me how to install the Supabase JavaScript client and create a client using environment variables for the project URL and public anon key.
3. Write the code to save a new <item> and to load the list of <items>.
4. Explain exactly which environment variables to add in Vercel and where.
5. Enable row level security on the table and write a basic policy that suits <who should read and write the data>.
Constraints: never expose the service role key in browser code, keep the code beginner friendly, and explain each step in plain English. Return the SQL, the code files with their names, and a short checklist for testing after deploying.
```
